lesson_title: Municipal Tariffs and Rising Block Systems: the Staircase on Your Bill
hook_text: 420 units of electricity. One family pays R954, the calculator says R1 029. The R75 gap is a staircase.
clip_script: Prepaid electricity is priced like a staircase. Your first 150 units this month stand on the cheap step — R1,95 each, that's R292,50. Units 151 and up climb to the next step — R2,45 each. Our household used 420 units: 150 on the bottom step, 270 on the second. R292,50 plus R661,50 — R954. Now watch the mistake half the country makes: 420 lands in block two, so multiply everything by R2,45? That's R1 029 — seventy-five rand wrong, because climbing higher never re-prices the cheap steps below you. Water works the same, except the bottom step is FREE — your first six thousand litres cost nothing. But a leaking toilet? That water sits on the TOP step, R29,50 a kilolitre plus VAT — the most expensive water in your house. And when someone offers you a flat-rate deal with a monthly fee, don't guess. Calculate both at YOUR usage. Small users win on the staircase; heavy users win on the flat rate. The crossing point is break-even. Know your steps, and the bill stops being a mystery.
visual_style: A staircase of glowing blocks rising across the screen, units stacking onto each step with prices stamped on the risers; a leaking toilet dripping coins onto the top step; two cost lines crossing at a break-even point drawn in chalk.
mood: Streetwise and protective, the voice of someone who reads the tariff table before loading the voucher.
pacing: Brisk up the staircase, a hard stop on the R1 029 mistake, slow and pointed on the free water and the break-even crossing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never overpay a municipal bill again.
